sections: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling

mechanism.owner_quote: Every request is authenticated and authorized at the resource boundary using principal identity, workload/device posture, policy and least privilege.
mechanism.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

invariant.owner_quote: Network location is not trust; a valid token is not object permission.
invariant.reason: States the no-implicit-trust rule and requires denied-path testing.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Policy gaps, legacy bypass paths and identity-provider outages are common.
failure_recovery.reason: External review 2026-10-27: binding does not support the full owner claim.

alternative.owner_quote: Network segmentation, a VPN or mTLS-only service identity may be preferable when legacy components cannot enforce per-request identity or when policy-evaluation cost exceeds the threat reduction.
alternative.reason: External review 2026-10-27: binding does not support the full owner claim.

sections: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling

mechanism.owner_quote: Least privilege grants each principal only the permissions its task needs, limited in resource scope, action and time.
mechanism.reason: Defines task-scoped permissions bounded by resource, action and time.

invariant.owner_quote: Every credential must have a bounded scope, an owner and a revocation path that does not depend on the compromised principal.
invariant.reason: Requires bounded scope, ownership and a revocation path independent of the principal.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Permission creep and long-lived credentials widen the blast radius without any visible incident; review grants on a schedule and prefer short-lived scoped credentials.
failure_recovery.reason: Names permission creep and long-lived credentials and requires scheduled review and short-lived credentials.

alternative.owner_quote: Coarse roles are simpler to administer for small stable systems; narrow them once measured access reviews or incident impact justify the overhead.
alternative.reason: ASVS Appendix D only recommends role allocation; no coarse-vs-narrow trade-off.

mechanism.owner_quote: A valet key is a scoped, time-limited credential that lets a client reach one resource directly.
mechanism.reason: Defines the scoped, time-limited direct-access credential.

invariant.owner_quote: It needs a least-privilege scope, an audience, an expiry, a revocation path and an audit trail.
invariant.reason: Lists the required scope, audience, expiry, revocation and audit properties.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is a leaked or over-scoped token; shorten lifetime, bind audience and scope, and revoke at the authority.
failure_recovery.reason: Describes the credential failure and its remediation.

alternative.owner_quote: A mediated gateway is the alternative when the resource cannot enforce scope or when the client cannot protect a credential.
alternative.reason: Names the competing mechanism and the conditions that favor it.

sections: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling

mechanism.owner_quote: Multitenant isolation keeps tenant data and effects separate inside a shared application by deriving tenant scope from authenticated context at every access path.
mechanism.reason: Derives tenant scope from authenticated context on every access path.

invariant.owner_quote: The tenant identifier must be derived from authentication and authorization, never accepted from an arbitrary caller field alone.
invariant.reason: ASVS 8.4.1 does not require tenant ID derived from authn/authz.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A missing tenant predicate in a query, cache or background task exposes another tenant's records; test indirect paths and enforce the predicate centrally.
failure_recovery.reason: ASVS has no missing-tenant-predicate or indirect-path test.

alternative.owner_quote: A tenant-per-deployment boundary removes shared-code risk at higher cost; share a deployment only when scoping is enforced consistently across every path.
alternative.reason: ASVS does not compare per-deployment isolation with shared scoping.

sections: When to use span events versus span attributes

mechanism.owner_quote: Distributed tracing reconstructs *a selected execution story*: a request enters a component, starts work, calls another component and may later complete asynchronously.
mechanism.reason: Explains tracing as reconstructing a selected cross-component execution story.

invariant.owner_quote: A trace can illuminate critical-path waiting, retries and failure propagation—but **it is not an authoritative record of every business effect**.
invariant.reason: OTel Traces page has no authoritative-record, missing-span or metrics/log comparison rule.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A missing span may mean no work occurred, the instrumentation failed, or the sampling policy intentionally discarded it.
failure_recovery.reason: OTel Traces page has no authoritative-record, missing-span or metrics/log comparison rule.

alternative.owner_quote: For aggregate latency or a discrete business event, metrics or structured logs may be preferable; use tracing when the cross-component path itself is the question.
alternative.reason: OTel Traces page has no authoritative-record, missing-span or metrics/log comparison rule.

sections: OpenTelemetry logs in the OpenTelemetry Collector

mechanism.owner_quote: Structured logging emits events with stable field names and types so records can be queried and compared without parsing free text.
mechanism.reason: Defines stable field names and types for queryable events.

invariant.owner_quote: Field names, meaning and redaction rules must be versioned, and sensitive values must be excluded before emission.
invariant.reason: External review 2026-10-27: binding does not support the full owner claim.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Schema drift or an unredacted field breaks queries or leaks data; validate the schema at the emitter and review field allowlists when adding events.
failure_recovery.reason: External review 2026-10-27: binding does not support the full owner claim.

alternative.owner_quote: Unstructured text parsed at query time is cheaper to start; adopt structured events when consistent querying, correlation or retention obligations justify the schema.
alternative.reason: Contrasts unstructured query-time parsing with structured events.

mechanism.owner_quote: A durable business audit records who attempted or authorized which object mutation and the resulting authoritative state, under a specified tamper and retention policy.
mechanism.reason: OpenLineage local text is only About page; no audit mutation/state content.

invariant.owner_quote: If legal obligations require atomic audit recording, architect the local commit or durable audit handoff explicitly; arbitrary asynchronous logs are insufficient.
invariant.reason: Text has no atomic audit recording or legal-retention rule.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The correct user outcome may still be committed; a missing log is not proof that booking disappeared.
failure_recovery.reason: Text has no missing-audit consequence or repair path.

alternative.owner_quote: If there is no mandatory forensic retention, costly immutable business audit infrastructure may be unnecessary for ordinary verbose debug logs.
alternative.reason: Text has no forensic-retention or debug-log alternative.

sections: What Do You and Your Users Care About?

mechanism.owner_quote: A hypothetical target SLO of 99.9% would allow at most 10 failures among 10,000 intents, while this window has 30, **consuming 300% of the target's error allowance**.
mechanism.reason: Shows how an objective converts user intents into an error budget and consumption.

invariant.owner_quote: Whether user cancellations, blocked abusive traffic, malformed requests and legitimate overload rejections count must be agreed before measurement; exclusion policy cannot change retrospectively to improve the score.
invariant.reason: States the required exclusions agreement and the no-retrospective-change rule.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: An instrumentation design that counts only HTTP 2xx responses among requests **admitted into the service**, excluding 500 deliberate overload rejections before the handler, can report misleading health.
failure_recovery.reason: Names the misleading denominator and required review.

alternative.owner_quote: Metrics or a simpler availability check may be preferable when the user journey is not measurable.
alternative.reason: Names simpler measurement and the reversal.

entries.unit: Monitoring Systems with Advanced Analytics — SRE Workbook
sections: Desirable Features of a Monitoring Strategy
Move information from logs to metrics
Keep logs as the data source

mechanism.owner_quote: Synthetic monitoring exercises a representative user journey from outside the service.
mechanism.reason: SRE chapter has no synthetic probes or external journeys.

invariant.owner_quote: It needs a safe identity, a journey definition, location and frequency choices and a rule that separates probe failure from product failure.
invariant.reason: Chapter has no probe identity, location or frequency rule.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is a probe that cannot authenticate or that tests only a trivial path; rotate credentials, cover the critical journey and triage probe noise separately.
failure_recovery.reason: Chapter has no probe-failure or credential remediation path.

alternative.owner_quote: Real-user monitoring is the alternative when actual traffic provides enough coverage without synthetic load.

entries.unit: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes — Kubernetes documentation
sections: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes
Use HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) with HTTP probes
Protect slow starting containers with startup probes

mechanism.owner_quote: Health checks answer different questions: liveness asks whether the process should be restarted, readiness asks whether it should receive traffic, and startup asks whether initialization has completed.
mechanism.reason: Explains the distinct liveness, readiness and startup decisions.

invariant.owner_quote: Each needs its own endpoint, timeout and failure action.
invariant.reason: Requires separate endpoints, timeouts and failure actions.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: The failure path is a false restart or traffic sent to an unready instance; bound probe timeouts, require consecutive failures and keep shared-dependency checks out of liveness.
failure_recovery.reason: Describes false-restart and unready-traffic failures with containment measures.

alternative.owner_quote: External journey monitoring is the alternative when process-local probes cannot observe the user-visible contract.
alternative.reason: Kubernetes page has only container-local probes, no external journey.
